criteria.name: Determinism gate
criteria.acceptanceRule: Candidate must preserve deterministic fixed-step outputs from canonical inputs across native, WASM, and supported browsers.

criteria.name: Worker isolation gate
criteria.acceptanceRule: Candidate must isolate heavy solving from the UI thread and support progress, cancellation, and stale-run rejection.

criteria.name: Offline workflow gate
criteria.acceptanceRule: After first successful online load, core edit/save/solve/replay workflows must remain available offline.

criteria.name: License compatibility gate
criteria.acceptanceRule: All required dependencies must use redistribution-compatible licenses.

criteria.name: Physics correctness, determinism, and numerical validation
criteria.acceptanceRule: Score 1-5 using deterministic kernel capability and numerical validation readiness.

criteria.name: Browser compatibility and offline behavior
criteria.acceptanceRule: Score 1-5 using support matrix fit and offline shell readiness.

criteria.name: Runtime responsiveness and performance
criteria.acceptanceRule: Score 1-5 using responsiveness architecture and benchmark feasibility.

criteria.name: Accessibility and rendered-output testability
criteria.acceptanceRule: Score 1-5 using DOM accessibility pathway and deterministic browser testability.

criteria.name: Maintainability and boundary clarity
criteria.acceptanceRule: Score 1-5 using ownership boundaries, migration clarity, and integration complexity.

criteria.name: Dependency maturity, security, and license posture
criteria.acceptanceRule: Score 1-5 using ecosystem maturity and known governance posture.

criteria.name: Debugging and observability
criteria.acceptanceRule: Score 1-5 using ability to inspect state, metrics, and failures reproducibly.

criteria.name: Build complexity and migration risk
criteria.acceptanceRule: Score 1-5 using build complexity, coupling, and long-term migration burden.

candidates.name: React + TypeScript + Vite with Rust/Rapier WASM in a dedicated worker

ratings.notes: Kernel design and deterministic feature set align with determinism requirements.
Dedicated worker architecture satisfies isolation, progress, and cancellation requirements.
Service worker plus IndexedDB supports first-load-then-offline workflow expectations.
Pinned dependencies use licenses compatible with browser redistribution.
Strongest support for deterministic coupled articulated dynamics in one kernel.
Static build and cache model fit browser matrix and offline constraints.
Off-main-thread architecture is strong; runtime target still requires measured benchmark proof.
Combines semantic DOM pathways with cross-browser automation and deterministic checks.
Clear boundaries, but Rust/WASM adds interface and toolchain maintenance overhead.
Selected dependencies are mature and pinned with established governance.
Good native/browser observability path with explicit validation artifacts.
Cross-language build introduces complexity and migration risk compared to pure TypeScript.

risks: Rust/WASM build complexity can slow onboarding and CI iteration.
Cross-language boundary drift between schema contracts and generated bindings must be controlled.
Performance targets remain provisional until benchmark and parity gates are measured.
candidates.fallback: Direct deterministic Rapier npm binding in worker with stricter deterministic preprocessing controls.

candidates.name: TypeScript app with deterministic Rapier npm binding in dedicated worker

ratings.notes: Deterministic engine exists, but preprocessing discipline still required.
Dedicated worker still isolates solve workload from UI.
Offline shell and persistence model are still achievable.
License posture appears compatible from package metadata.
Strong engine, but deterministic preprocessing split across TypeScript and WASM raises risk.
Browser/offline story remains strong.
Similar isolation profile, though data marshaling paths differ.
Good testability baseline; fewer explicit cross-language constraints documented.
Mixed responsibility for deterministic preprocessing weakens boundary clarity.
Mature dependencies, but less explicit coverage for physics boundary ownership.
Debugging remains practical, but deterministic root-cause analysis may span runtimes.
Simpler build chain than Rust/WASM, but long-term determinism risk remains.

risks: Deterministic preprocessing outside Rust may introduce cross-platform drift.
Boundary ownership for authoritative physics values is less strict.
Validation burden increases for parity and canonical math enforcement.
candidates.fallback: Promote deterministic preprocessing and analysis logic into a Rust kernel if drift appears.

candidates.name: Main-thread TypeScript-first stack with lightweight physics integration

ratings.notes: Fails hard determinism confidence because deterministic ownership is fragmented.
Fails required off-main-thread solve isolation and cancellation responsiveness expectations.
Offline shell and storage are possible.
No license blocker identified from baseline metadata.
Cannot demonstrate the same confidence in deterministic coupled physics execution.
Browser compatibility can be good but does not compensate failed hard gates.
Main-thread solve contention conflicts with responsiveness targets.
UI-level a11y can be addressed, but solver architecture remains incompatible with constraints.
Boundary clarity weakens due to tightly coupled simulation and presentation concerns.
Dependencies may be mature, but architectural fit is poor.
Debugging non-deterministic contention across UI and simulation paths is harder.
Simpler initial build, but future migration to compliant architecture is likely.

risks: Fails mandatory worker isolation and deterministic ownership gates.
High risk of UI responsiveness regressions under heavy solve workloads.
Would require architectural rework before compliant production rollout.
